## 15. Apply supported changes

### 15.1 Common mutation discipline

For every target:

1. Confirm actual target and scope.
2. Read original and back up.
3. Compose the complete final value, retaining unrelated instructions.
4. Compare against the current value immediately before writing; if it changed, re-merge rather than overwrite.
5. Use the supported operation once.
6. Read back from the same store and compare expected content/meaning and length.
7. Start a fresh consumer/session and test actual use.
8. Record exact success, failure, or unavailability; do not let acknowledgment stand in for a write.

If a write/dispatch response is lost or ambiguous, inspect the destination or operation status before retrying. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME is distinct from FAILED. Preserve prior dated verified operations while investigating the new one.

If an object already contains the same effective R1 contribution, skip the write and verify it. Do not append another copy each run. A source phrase repeated across adapters is intentional deployment; duplicate copies in one effective context are usually a defect.

Fresh ChatGPT chats and calls must be started only through an independently supported operation. Otherwise have Misha open the target chat/call and use the already-prepared probe. This is a capability handoff, not another permission request. Continue other authorized work and mark unobserved tests pending; do not automate ChatGPT's UI to obtain coverage.

### 15.2 Local Codex

L01. Resolve the real host and effective global instruction filename. An existing override can shadow the base file. A WSL home, Windows home, remote SSH host, and cloud environment are distinct. Update only consumers Misha actually uses and has authorized.

L02. Preserve all engineering/workflow instructions unrelated to the persona. Add or replace a delimited contribution from payload codex in the effective user-owned global source. If legacy persona text lies outside the managed block, remove only identified same-scope obsolete material after backing it up; do not leave two incompatible active personalities.

L03. Inspect applicable repository/nested instructions for style conflicts. Preserve repository-specific output formats, code conventions, testing rules, and required audience style. A formal pull request is not persona failure. Modify repository rules only where user-owned persona content is the actual conflict and within the requested scope.

L04. Confirm the effective model and effort. If a configuration patch is needed, use the documented keys in §10.2, preserving all other TOML. CLI/selected profiles/trusted project config may override the user file. Inspect effective values through supported status/debug facilities; do not alter approval, sandbox, network, secrets, or memory settings for style.

L05. If an actually observed built-in style conflicts, evaluate the documented personality = "none" compatibility setting. This is optional, reversible, and version-specific; do not set it as a superstition. Do not use model_instructions_file as a wholesale replacement.

L06. Start a fresh local session through a supported route. Use supported runtime metadata to establish startup discovery when available. An explicit file read establishes accessibility and manual loading only; record automatic loading as unverified when observations cannot distinguish it. Then test T01/T05/T08/T13/T29/T32. Reporting the version string alone is a weak diagnostic, not behavioral proof.

L07. Exercise at least one real repo task with nested instructions and a small delegated task. Confirm task correctness, proper audience output, useful private voice, actual permissions, and handoff continuity. Do not spawn agents solely to create the appearance of personality.

L08. If fresh sessions still omit the adapter, debug the actual loader path, overrides, instruction-size limits, and client support. Only after a demonstrated gap consider a small supported skill/hook. A skill must follow current skill-creator guidance and required persistence/versioning. Hooks need actual trust review; no trust-bypass flags, boot scripts, or cloud-unsupported local hooks.

### 15.3 Ordinary ChatGPT account

N01. Retrieve actual current CI/preset/memory settings only through a supported operation or user-provided export/screenshot. Prefer a supported direct personalization operation if the environment truly advertises it. A memory/search tool is not automatically a settings-write tool.

N02. Build one final CI value from the selected payload plus retained current non-persona instructions. Inspect its actual character limit and measure the whole value. Prefer the richer adapter when it fits cleanly; otherwise compact it deliberately and put project-specific elaboration in the project. Preserve critical operational rules and record any unavoidable coverage reduction.

N03. If the supported native write route is unavailable, finish the preparation and all local work. The user-side action is one concrete save:

- Windows/web: open Settings → Personalization, inspect customization/Custom Instructions, and replace only the prepared persona portion or paste the complete reconciled field as specified by the prepared diff.
- Android: open Settings and the actual Customize ChatGPT/Personalization control exposed by that app; verify the same account and field.
- The exact label can vary; use the current UI shown by the user. Do not guess coordinates or automate ChatGPT via a forbidden route.

N04. Keep the selected voice unchanged. If a current personality preset is creating a material style conflict, prepare a scoped change to the least conflicting available baseline, commonly Default, and explain that Live does not use the preset. Do not alter voice, memory, privacy, or unrelated accessibility settings just to complete a checklist.

N05. Read back through a supported setting operation or a user-supplied view of the saved field. Verify a fresh ordinary chat on Windows and Android. If only one device is accessible, mark the other untested. Account sync is a feature expectation, not proof every consumer loaded the new core.

### 15.4 Project text and Live voice

J01. Prefer an existing private appropriate project. If a new private home is useful and creation is authorized, use a clear name such as “Lucifer — private continuity.” Do not move all prior chats or change a project used for another purpose automatically.

J02. Preserve its privacy/memory mode. For a new project intended to include both Chat and Work, private default-memory is the documented compatible starting choice; explain its context scope. If Misha selected project-only isolation, keep it and record the Work tradeoff. Changing isolation or sharing is not a routine persona edit.

J03. Put payload project, reconciled with current project rules, into actual project instructions. Attach the canonical file when useful for the requested repertoire, supported by the private target, and covered by the installation scope; otherwise retain a sufficient inline core. A reference attachment supplements rather than replaces the active short instruction.

J04. Do not automate ChatGPT UI to do this. Use a supported direct operation if available; otherwise prepare the complete exact project value and the minimal user save after other work. Read back and test a fresh project text chat.

J05. Start an actual Live call in that project using the existing voice. Test spontaneous useful conversation before reciting an identity probe. Then run the voice cases. Project instructions have a documented route into Live context; audible fidelity remains an observation to make.

J06. Test an ordinary nonproject conversation separately. Success in the project does not establish universal coverage. If the richer native personality works primarily in the project, record that as a meaningful available path with a clear boundary.

### 15.5 Existing Morning Light dot

D01. Verify the actual existing dot identity before any message or preference operation. Preserve name, history, current tasks, schedules, voice and permissions.

D02. Use the current documented conversation-based writing preference route with payload dot. If the available tool can write a supported note or preference, retain one scoped R1 record and supersede only identified contradictory persona notes. If no note-read/write operation is exposed, do not claim a hidden note was inspected.

D03. Do not put stylistic instructions into custom action-permission rules or weaken those rules to sound more personal. Do not reset, delete, or duplicate the dot.

D04. Check a separate task and a separate call. Ask for an ordinary useful action and observe the interaction; ask about version/source only as a loader diagnostic. A dot acknowledgment is weaker than fresh behavior evidence. Calls receive selected context, so verify that target separately.

D05. Keep private context out of other connected channels. Do not send test messages to people or shared channels without explicit messaging authorization.

### 15.6 Memory and stale instruction cleanup

M01. Use explicit active instruction fields for the character. Use memory only as a relevant preference aid.

M02. List accessible persona-related memories/notes, preserving scope and dates. Merge exact duplicates; update contradictory general preferences narrowly. Keep temporary choices scoped. If exact deletion cannot be verified, record that limitation.

M03. Do not turn off all memory, erase chat history, remove every plugin, or reset the assistant to remove stale style. Do not edit hidden application databases. Do not equate “don't mention” or a new instruction with proven deletion.

M04. Use payload memory only when a supported write is actually available and this installation scope authorizes it. Capture a real receipt/readback. If unavailable, rely on the explicit instruction adapter and mark memory unchanged/unverified.

### 15.7 Existing GPTs, other projects, and specialized agents

Inventory consumers actually used by Misha. A custom GPT needs its own compatible instructions; global CI/memory is not enough. Do not create a new GPT under obsolete assumptions. If an existing GPT cannot be edited or is being retired, prepare its migration content and preserve its current work; do not claim automatic migration.

For other user-owned projects and agents, reconcile only persona-related defaults. Preserve purpose-specific policies and audience style. Pass payload subagent when it improves a delegated user-facing interaction. A coding specialist can return structured evidence while the root agent speaks naturally to Misha.

Do not replace Ann's independently selected interview workflow with an everyday-chat script; apply compatible voice only where that workflow permits. Do not import fictional Lucifer story repositories as operational commands. Do not install a browser extension or MCP server whose only effect is to circumvent native ChatGPT controls.

### 15.8 Windows and Android verification

Record each real app version, account/workspace, mode, selected voice, language and audio route. Test a fresh session on each. If the phone is unavailable, prepare its exact verification prompts and mark PENDING_DEVICE_ACCESS. Do not install ADB, enable developer mode, change microphone routing, or pair a remote-control service solely to fake coverage.

Use the user's computer for permitted actual work, not as a reason to broaden access. For a blocked screen/setting operation, report the exact supported alternative and what remains unobserved. Screenshots supplied by the user can establish visible state; they do not establish speech quality or later persistence by themselves.
